item.title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
item.description: We develop neural network methods for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations at a small viscosity $\varepsilon > 0$, whose accuracy is uniform in $\varepsilon$ and whose residual is evaluated on a grid that does not resolve the vorticity boundary layer. In the vorticity-stream function formulation with the slip boundary conditions, a vorticity layer of width $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ forms along the walls. The trial function of the singular layer Physics-Informed Neural Network (sl-PINN) contains… — Teng-Yuan Chang, Gung-Min Gie, Youngjoon Hong, Chang-Yeol Jung — arXiv: navier

item.title: Forward Self-similar Solutions of the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in Dimensions Five and Higher
item.description: We construct forward self-similar solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 5$) for arbitrary $(-1)$-homogeneous, divergence-free initial data $u_0$ smooth on the unit sphere. For $n\ge 6$, the $O(|y|^{-3})$ bound on the nonlinear residual of the linear heat profile no longer yields $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$-integrability, obstructing a direct global energy perturbation around $e^Δu_0$. To overcome this difficulty, we truncate $u_0$ near the origin via a divergence-free cutoff… — Baishun Lai, Ruiyi Zhang, Xiaoxin Zheng — arXiv: navier

item.title: An Explicit Parallelizable Robin-Robin Splitting Scheme for Navier-Stokes-Naghdi Shell Interaction
item.description: We develop a novel explicit Robin-Robin splitting scheme for the system of an incompressible viscous fluid coupled to a time dependent Naghdi shell model. The shell model includes three displacement components and three independent rotation components, accounting for membrane, bending, and transverse-shear deformations. Both Robin conditions depend only on interface data from the previous time step, allowing the fluid and shell subproblems to be solved independently without coupling subiterations. For the… — Yifan Wang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
item.description: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that… — Shuo Fan — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
item.description: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=\lambda(1+t)^{-\mu}$ with $0<\mu<1$, $\lambda>0$, or $\mu=1$, $\lambda>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the… — Yuusuke Sugiyama — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Counterexamples to Ecker's Conjecture
item.description: Analogous to Perelman's W-entropy defined for Ricci flow, K. Ecker defined a functional W for the mean curvature flow in R^{n+1} and the region it encloses, and made the conjecture that this functional is monotonically increasing in time. In this paper, we give a negative answer to Ecker's conjecture. — Jiarui Chen, Jie Wang — arXiv: ricci

item.title: The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
item.description: We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam. — Jnaneshwar Baslingker, Daniel Spivak, Balint Virag — arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
item.description: We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. For a fixed weak nonzero shock, sufficiently weak rarefaction and contact waves, and small H^2(R) initial perturbations, we establish asymptotic stability with a time-dependent shift on the viscous shock. The L^4 time average of the uniform perturbation and the shift velocity over [t,2t] is bounded by C_S(1+t)^(-1/4). We prove pointwise-in-time… — Le Chen — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA / arXiv: navier

item.title: Invariant solitons of the inverse mean curvature flow in the sphere and in hyperbolic space
item.description: We study hypersurfaces of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ and of hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, $n\ge 3$, that move under the inverse mean curvature flow by a one-parameter group of isometries. No closed hypersurface has this property, and a soliton with constant mean curvature is an open subset of a horosphere. For the rotation hypersurfaces of do Carmo and Dajczer, of spherical, hyperbolic and parabolic type, the soliton equation reduces to a single ordinary differential equation, which we analyse in every… — Hiuri Fellipe Santos dos Reis, Levi Rosa Adriano, Miriam Cristina Ferreira Furtado — arXiv math.DG / MG / GN / GR / QA / arXiv: ricci

item.title: Finite element nonlinear nudging for the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: Nonlinear nudging augments the classical linear nudging (continuous data as- similation) term with a nonlinear feedback that strengthens as the observed error decreases, and yields super-exponential convergence to the true state. In this paper, we study nonlinear nudging for the 3-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the finite element method, which allows complex geometries and physical boundary conditions. We propose an implicit-explicit (IMEX) finite element scheme with inf-sup stable… — Elizabeth Carlson, Rui Fang, Ali Pakzad — arXiv: navier

item.title: Boundary $ C^2, \gamma $ regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s MTW condition
item.description: We establish boundary regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s Ma--Trudinger--Wang condition. Let the source and target be bounded, mutually $ c $-convex domains in $ \mathbb{R}^n $, $ n\geqslant2 $, with $ C^{1,\beta} $ boundaries, and suppose that the cost is smooth, bi-twisted, and nondegenerate. For positive $ C^{0,\alpha} $ densities bounded away from zero and having equal total mass, we prove that both Kantorovich potentials belong to $ C^{2,\gamma} $ up to the boundary, where $ \gamma =… — Yizhong Hong, Feng Wang — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Moment approximations in optimal transport: geometric estimates and a semiclassical limit
item.description: We study finite moment approximations of linear optimization problems over measures. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the existence of discrete minimizers with a controlled number of support points, duality and $\Gamma$-convergence as the moment approximation is refined. This framework accommodates several transport problems, in which marginal constraints are replaced by finitely many moment constraints. For moment functions localized at scale $r_n$, we prove an estimate controlling $W_\infty$ by $W_p$ up… — Luigi de Pascale, Luca Nenna, Igor Pinheiro — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA / arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Combinatorial Properties of The Giant Under Supercritical Percolation
item.description: We study combinatorial properties, such as diameter and long paths and cycles, of the giant component of percolated graphs. Such combinatorial properties are well studied for classical graphs such as pseudo-random graphs and the hypercube. We aim to obtain similar results for extensive families of $d$-regular $n$-vertex graphs. Specifically, assuming expansion properties of the host graph, we show a typical vertex expansion by a factor of $1/d\log d$ in the giant component of the percolated subgraph. As a… — Sahar Diskin, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Itay Markbreit — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS / arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Isometrically greedy renormings of bidemocratic unconditional bases of Banach spaces
item.description: We show that if a greedy basis of a Banach space has the additional property that its dual basis is also greedy, then the space admits an equivalent norm under which the basis is isometrically greedy. This solves in the positive a question posed by Dilworth, Kutzarova, Odell, Schlumprecht and Zs\'ak in 2014. As an application, we resolve a long-standing problem explicitly posed by Albiac, Ansorena and Wallis in 2017 by proving that any subsymmetric basis of a Banach space is isometrically greedy under a suitable… — Alejandro Marcos, Jose L. Ansorena — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Heat-wave semigroup estimates and the compressible Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: We study the connection between the heat-wave semigroup and the compressible Navier-Stokes (CNS) equations. On one hand, the parabolic-hyperbolic nature of the CNS motivated the study of space-time estimates for the heat-wave semigroup by using recent harmonic analysis development, in particular, the local smoothing estimates for the wave equations; on the other hand, we apply the new estimates to obtain global well-posedness for CNS in the optimal critical Besov spaces. For the latter purpose, we introduce a new… — Rongshan Chen, Zihua Guo — arXiv: navier

item.title: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
item.description: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that… — José Gomes, Matheus Hudson, Raquel Lemos — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
item.description: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive. Here, we treat the QAOA distribution as a statistical-physics object and probe its geometry directly in the thermodynamic limit. We draw two independent bitstrings from the same problem instance and… — Maxime Dupont, Bhuvanesh Sundar — arXiv: spin glass

item.title: Vanishing Dissipation Limit to Planar Euler Shock for the Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations in $\mathbbR^3$
item.description: We prove the vanishing dissipation limit to a weak planar Euler shock for the full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The viscosity and heat conductivity are proportional to $\varepsilon$, with their ratio fixed. The conservative initial perturbation may depend on all three spatial variables and is assumed small only in the scaled $H^2 \cap \dot H^{-1}$ norm. No $L^1$ bound or zero-mass condition is required. For these data, we obtain a unique global strong solution and an energy estimate… — Yujie Wang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
item.description: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For… — Huy The Nguyen, Artemis A. Vogiatzi — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA / arXiv math.DG / MG / GN / GR / QA / arXiv: ricci

item.title: VOL-Agent: Programming Your Film via Video Orchestration Language Agentic System
item.description: Recent video foundation models generate high-quality and limited-length clips, but orchestrating them into minute-level, story-coherent films remains an open problem. Existing video agents highly rely on natural-language planning or predefined workflows, which make their production hard to program, customize, and extend. Therefore, we introduce VOL-Agent, a programmable video agent built on a Video Orchestration Language (VOL). With static compilation and verification, followed by runtime dynamic loading… — Hongji Yang, Yucheng Zhou, Lingting Zhu, Shengju Qian, Xinye Li, Huan Zheng — arXiv: kakeya

item.title: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
item.description: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$. — Hanbing Fang, Yongheng Han — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system with general bulk viscosity and Navier slip boundary conditions
item.description: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with Navier slip boundary conditions is established in a smooth bounded domain that may be multiply connected. Arbitrarily large initial data and vacuum are allowed, and the positive doping profile may have large spatial variations. item.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
item.description: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on… — Heiko Knospe, Jiahe Shen, Roger Van Peski — arXiv: random matrix / arXiv: riemann

item.title: Time-decay rates toward viscous shock waves for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system
item.description: We study small H^2(R) perturbations of a fixed weak viscous 3-shock for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system. For each fixed initial perturbation, the error from the shifted profile in the uniform norm and the shift velocity are o(t^{-1/4}). Nearby stationary profiles give spatial estimates in terms of the time derivative. Estimates along the characteristics bound the perturbation at time t by the dissipation on [t/2, t]. The exponent 1/4 is sharp for a uniform bound on the small H^2 ball. — Le Chen, Yujie Wang — arXiv: navier

item.title: From a High-T$m_C$ Spin-Gapless Semiconductor to a Spin-Glass: The Role of Disorder in NiMnCrAl
item.description: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. For the ordered Y-type structure, density-functional-theory calculations predict a ferrimagnetic spin-gapless-semiconducting state with a total magnetic moment of $1.99\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}/\mathrm{f.u.}$ and a mean-field ordering temperature of approximately $1300~\mathrm{K}$. Polycrystalline NiMnCrAl forms in a single average cubic… — Arka Patra, Tufan Roy, Nilofar Kurawle, Tamaghna Maitra, Souvik Banerjee, Mantu Modak — arXiv: spin glass

item.title: Canonical spin glass behavior and memory effects in van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2
item.description: We demonstrate the canonical spin-glass behavior and non-equilibrium dynamics in a single-crystalline Ni-doped van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2 with a freezing temperature $T_f \approx 45.5$ K from detailed ac susceptibility and dc magnetization measurements. The temperature-dependent dc magnetization exhibits strong magnetic irreversibility and the ac susceptibility shows that the peak at $T_f$ shifts towards higher temperatures with increase in ac frequency, indicating the presence of a spin glass… — P. Biswal, Kakan Deb, Nitesh Kumar, D. Samal, Prabhat Mandal — arXiv: spin glass

item.title: Edge behavior of the KPZ fixed point under upper-tail conditioning
item.description: We consider the KPZ fixed point $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(x,t)$ with the narrow-wedge initial profile, conditioned on $\{\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{KPZ}}(0,1)\ge L\}$ as $L\to\infty$. Our main result describes its fluctuations near the boundary of the region affected by the conditioning. More precisely, in the spatial window $x=t\sqrt L+O(1)$, the centered field converges in finite-dimensional distributions to the KPZ fixed point with a half-Brownian initial profile. The convergence holds jointly at arbitrary… — Yuanyuan Liu, Zhipeng Liu, Haoyang Ying — arXiv: kpz prob

item.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
item.description: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover for strictly positive initial… — Xinyu Fan, Song Jiang, Jing Li, Boqiang Lv — arXiv: navier

item.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
item.description: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other… — Benjamin Joseph, Tamás Keleti, Márk Kökényesi, András Máthé, Andrew Schmidt — arXiv: kakeya

item.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
item.description: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and… — William Verreault, Max Wenqiang Xu — arXiv: random matrix

item.title: Tightness of bulk crossing heights for the planar discrete Gaussian free field
item.description: Let $φ_N$ be the planar discrete Gaussian free field in $[-2N,2N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with zero boundary condition imposed by killing the associated simple random walk on exit. We consider the least height $H_N$ at which the two-sided level set $\{|φ_N|\leq a\}$ contains a nearest-neighbor left--right crossing of $[-N,N]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. item.title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: We develop two hybrid data-driven Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) Reduced-Order Models (ROMs) for the non-stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes Equations (NSEs) with random viscosity. The proposed framework combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) ROMs, spatial filtering, data-driven closure modeling, and the Stochastic Collocation Method (SCM). A key feature is the approximation of the realization-dependent closure term by the closure associated with the expected viscosity. Consequently, a single… — Md. Abdul Aziz, Muhammad Mohebujjaman, Xuping Xie — arXiv: navier

item.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
item.description: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. item.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
item.description: For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every Hölder space $C^α$, $α<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $α=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. item.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
item.description: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. item.title: A posteriori space error estimates for the finite element approximation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations based on the variational multiscale framework
item.description: This study introduces a novel a posteriori space error estimator derived within the variational multiscale (VMS) framework for the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this framework, the continuous problem is decomposed into coarse and fine scales. The fine scale, often referred to as the sub-grid scale (SGS), is modeled as proportional to the component of the residual orthogonal to the finite element (FE) space. This modeled SGS then serves as a reliable error estimator. Specifically, the… — Javad Sekhavati, Ignacio Martínez-Suárez, Sheraz Ahmed Khan, Joan Baiges, Guillermo Hauke, Ramon Codina — arXiv: navier

item.title: Physical interpretation of spin-glass models with correlated disorder
item.description: Ising spin-glass models with a specific type of correlated bond disorder have recently been used to relate properties of spin-glass phases, such as temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos, to ferromagnetic order. item.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
item.description: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. item.title: On regularity and stability results of global weak solutions to two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum
item.description: For the initial and initial-boundary value problems of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum, Lions' global weak solutions are shown to possess additional regularity, via establishing some key a priori decay-in-time rates for the approximate problem, under suitable smallness condition on the density-dependent viscosity. In addition, large-time decay rates of the pressure and gradient of velocity are obtained, which are even exponential in time… — Yanfang Peng, Hongyu Wang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
item.description: Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial… — Zhengyan Wu, Ao Zhang — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Spin-glass order in a field requires magnetic-field chaos in XY gauge glasses for $d\leq 4$
item.description: The XY gauge-glass model is believed to exhibit a spin-glass phase in dimensions $d\geq 3$. In this paper, we prove that, in dimensions $d\leq 4$ and at any finite temperature, a magnetic field applied in a fixed direction, with amplitudes that fluctuate from site to site according to the Rayleigh distribution, must either induce magnetic-field chaos in the spin-glass phase or destroy spin-glass order altogether, whenever a spin-glass phase exists at zero field. item.title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
item.description: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. item.title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass
item.description: When an AI diffusion-type generator samples a frustrated spin glass, which macroscopic alternatives does it decide first, and when? We study this for bridge-diffusion models of the Path Integral Diffusion (PID) type started from a point source. We show that every isotropic PID is a time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization, and conversely every signal-to-noise schedule is realized by a PID protocol. item.title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
item.description: Physics-informed neural networks(PINNs) offer a mesh-free and continuously differentiable approach to fluid simulation. However, standard monolithic PINNs for incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations often suffer from severe constraint coupling and spectral biases, limiting both convergence and accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose a segregated, iterative, and multi-stage PINN (SIM-PINN) inspired by the classical projection method in computational fluid dynamics. In SIM-PINN, the nonlinear NS… — Zhenyu Zhang, Zhixiang Ling, Yinghao Huo, Huayong Liu, Yunde Su — arXiv: kakeya / arXiv: navier

item.title: Navier-Stokes characteristic boundary conditions for the Spectral Difference method on simplex elements
item.description: Unsteady compressible simulations with high-order methods on unstructured meshes require boundaries that let acoustic, entropy and vorticity waves leave the domain without spurious reflection. For the spectral difference (SD) method, the Navier-Stokes characteristic boundary conditions (NSCBC) have only been formulated on quadrilaterals and hexahedra. Their strong-form formalism relies on a line of flux points normal to the boundary face, which does not exist on triangles and tetrahedra. item.title: Extensions to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations for Rarefied Transport: Entropy Variable Formulation, Heat Transfer and Dispersion of a Non-Linear Entropy Stable Closure
item.description: We assess the non-linear version of the Entropy Stable Extension to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations which were originally derived in arXiv:2407.17334. Using an identity for the derivative of the inverse of linearized collision operator, we show that the Entropy Stable Extension takes the form of a fourth-order quasi-cubic system of equations when written in entropy variables. Furthermore, we find that the quasi-linear contributions to the extension retain the highest order derivative contributions and the… — Frimpong A. Baidoo, Narayana R. Aluru, Thomas J. R. Hughes, Michael R. A. Abdelmalik — arXiv: navier

item.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4π$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass $m<4π$, the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for $m>4π$, there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated… — Lili Du, Yulan Wang, Yichen Zhang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
item.description: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge… — Wei-Chun Chen, Chun-Kai Lien — arXiv: ricci

item.title: The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
item.description: A hard edge of a Hermitian random matrix occurs when the eigenvalue density is strictly zero on one side of the edge, and nonzero on the other. Another possibility is that the eigenvalues occur in $\pm$ pairs, which creates a hard edge at the origin for the positive eigenvalues. Both review material and new results are presented for random matrix ensembles exhibiting a hard edge. The review material has two focuses: one is on applications of the random matrix hard edge, while the other is on exact eigenvalue… — Peter J. Forrester, Anas A. Rahman, Bo-Jian Shen — arXiv: random matrix

item.title: $a$-contraction applied to the time-asymptotic stability of weak shocks for a general 1-D viscous system
item.description: The method of $a$-contraction with shifts builds on the relative entropy method of Dafermos and DiPerna and allows both viscous shocks and rarefaction waves to be studied directly at the level of the solution. This unified framework led to the resolution of Matsumura's long-standing conjecture on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous shock in composition with a rarefaction. Kang, Vasseur, and Wang established this stability for the one-dimensional compressible barotropic Navier-Stokes system. Their result… — Young-Sam Kwon, Jiayun Meng, Alexis Vasseur — arXiv: navier

item.title: Singular viscosity-exponent limit for one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with far field vacuum
item.description: We consider the limit $δ\to1^+$ for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity $μ(ρ)=ρ^δ$ and far field vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result on the viscosity-exponent limit $δ\to1^+$ for strong solutions with far field vacuum. With far field vacuum, the diffusion coefficient $ρ^{δ-1}$ does not converge uniformly to $1$ on $\mathbb R$ as $δ\to1^+$. The main difficulty is to obtain uniform estimates for this limit. By introducing some new weighted density… — Xingyang Zhang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
item.description: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it. This stems from a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing the zero-field endpoint is exactly pinned while the characteristic finite-quench… — Giuseppe D'Auria, Alessandro Silva — arXiv: spin glass

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of generic Riemann solutions to one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations
item.description: This paper investigates the time-asymptotic stability of the one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, assuming that the corresponding quasi-neutral Euler equations admit a generic Riemann solution consisting of a shock, a contact discontinuity, and a rarefaction wave. It is proved that there exists a unique global-in-time solution, which converges in $L^\infty$ norm, as time goes to infinity, to the ansatz composed of a viscous shock with a time-dependent shift, a viscous contact wave… — Xin-Xiang Bian, Jiajin Shi, Lingling Xie — arXiv: navier

item.title: From Navier-Stokes to Measure-Valued Euler-Brinkman Equations: Homogenization in the Inviscid Limit
item.description: We study the behaviour of the solution to the Navier-Stokes equations with vanishing viscosity and a no-slip condition in a periodically perforated domain. The behaviour depends on the particle size and the viscosity of the fluid. We prove convergence to a measure-valued solution, provided that the local Reynolds number is small, in the subcritical and critical regime. In the first case, the limit solves the Euler equations, whereas in the second case it solves the Euler-Brinkman equations. This extends the… — Richard M. Höfer, Eleni Hübner-Rosenau — arXiv: navier

item.title: Large time behavior of global solutions to one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations with large initial data
item.description: In this paper, we are concerned with the construction of global solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, as well as the precise description of their large-time behavior. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. Even for constant transport coefficients, only the Nishida-Smoller type solutions have been obtained so far. In this work, we will provide a… — Lan Zhang, Huijiang Zhao — arXiv: navier

item.title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $ε^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
item.description: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $ε$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $ε$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $ε^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly… — Haijun Gao, Xi Li, Xiaoli Li — arXiv: navier

item.title: Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof
item.description: In this note, we give a short probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation of the stationary measure of the open Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, conjectured by Barraquand and Le Doussal and recently established in full generality by Dunlap, Gu and Rosati. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation of the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) under Liggett's condition, together… — Dominik Schmid, Zongrui Yang — arXiv: kpz prob

item.title: On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
item.description: We consider the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on the cable system of a transient weighted graph with volume growth exponent $α$ and Green function decay exponent $ν$. We prove that the probability that the cluster of a vertex reaches distance $R$ is of order $R^{-β}$ when $2α<3ν$, where $β=α-ν$ is the walk dimension, and that the same holds up to a logarithmic factor in the upper bound when $2α=3ν$. On $\mathbb Z^d$ these conditions read $d>6$ and $d=6$. The upper bound combines a general entropic… — Pierre-François Rodriguez, Jialu Shi, Wen Zhang — arXiv: sle

item.title: On knotted self expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\R^3$
item.description: In this article we produce many examples of knotted self expanders. For example, there is an expander isotopic to a trefoil knot with three half cylinders attached. — Alexander Mramor, Shengwen Wang — arXiv: ricci

item.title: On the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space
item.description: In this paper, we study the anisotropic mean curvature flow in the Gaussian space endowed with a Finsler metric obtained from a Minkowski metric by a conformal deformation. We first derive the conformal transformation formulas for the fundamental tensor, the Cartan tensor, and the Chern connection of the conformally related Finsler metrics. Based on these formulas, we express the anisotropic mean curvature in the Gaussian space in terms of the corresponding anisotropic mean curvature with respect to the original… — Di Zhang — arXiv: ricci

item.title: The anelastic approximation and convergence rate for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with ill-prepared data in bounded domains
item.description: We justify the anelastic approximation and establish a convergence rate for local strong solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with ill-prepared initial data and vorticity-slip boundary conditions. When the Mach and Froude numbers vanish at the same rate $ε$, the system converges to an anelastic system with nonconstant hydrostatic density. Compared with the incompressible limit, the balance between singular pressure and gravity generates a… — Yaobin Ou, Ping Wang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
item.description: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$… — Zhen Lei, Xiao Ren — arXiv: navier

item.title: 2D Navier-Stokes with viscosity-dependent Navier slip: strong convergence for unbounded initial velocity
item.description: For the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with Navier friction on a smooth, bounded, simply connected domain, we establish strong vorticity convergence along a subsequence in the vanishing viscosity limit for initial vorticity in $L^p$ with $p>1$. The friction coefficients may grow as viscosity vanishes under an explicit growth restriction depending on $p$, which includes regimes of vanishing slip length. The main challenge, even for viscosity-independent friction, is to control the vorticity… — Josef Demmel — arXiv: navier

item.title: Global Stability and Decay for the 2D Anisotropic Navier-Stokes Equations with Fractional Horizontal Dissipation
item.description: Although the classical Yudovich theory guarantees global existence and uniqueness of two-dimensional Euler solutions with bounded vorticity, their higher-order norms may still grow in time. This raises a fundamental question: how much dissipation we need to ensure global stability and decay? While the full Laplacian dissipation is sufficient, the stabilizing effect of weaker, anisotropic dissipation is considerably more subtle. In this paper, we investigate the global stability and long-time decay of the… — Chenyan Shen, Dan Wu, Yi Zhu — arXiv: navier

item.title: Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature
item.description: In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities… — Maxwell Stolarski, Wei-Bo Su — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations by One Noise Component
item.description: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the torus with multiplicative Itô noise which is driven by a single Brownian motion and acts only through the vertical velocity component. Such a noise is strongly degenerate: An infinite-dimensional part of the velocity field is not forced at all. We show that it nevertheless has a regularizing effect. For a linear noise, strong solutions whose initial data have no unforced part are global with probability tending to one as the noise… — Felix Brandt, Igor Kukavica — arXiv: navier

item.title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
item.description: We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble converges for each $β>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $β$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrtβ$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu. — Vadim Gorin, Lingfu Zhang — arXiv: sle

item.title: Glauber dynamics of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model: a dynamical cavity method
item.description: We present a closed theory, exact in the $N\to\infty$ limit, of the equilibrium spin correlations of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model evolving with Glauber dynamics, above and at the transition temperature $T_c$. The derivation uses a dynamic cavity approach: in the evolution equation for the selected spin the other spins are represented by a fluctuating field. The influence of the selected spin on this field is included at the linear response level; it is given as a sum of the spin's past flips… — Grzegorz Szamel — arXiv: spin glass

item.title: Supercritical level-set percolation on finite graphs
item.description: We continue the study of bond percolation on finite graphs induced by the level-sets of the zero-average Gaussian free field on the associated metric graph. In our previous work Goswami and Pal (2026), we analyzed the critical and near-critical behavior of this model on uniform expanders, focusing on the volume of the largest cluster. In the present paper, we investigate the size of the second largest cluster in the supercritical regime --- the phase where one expects a unique giant component. We prove that the… — Subhajit Goswami, Dipranjan Pal — arXiv: sle

item.title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
item.description: We study a fundamental problem in machine learning: partial recovery of a planted signal $\boldsymbol{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ from a spiked tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}} = λ\, \boldsymbol{v}^{\otimes p} + \boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ has symmetric Gaussian entries of variance $\asymp n^{-1}$. While previous works replace $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ by an i.i.d. standard Gaussian tensor to circumvent technical difficulties caused by dependencies, this paper directly analyzes the… — Tom Szwagier, Xiaoyi Mai, José Henrique de Morais Goulart — arXiv: random matrix

item.title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation
item.description: We determine the monochromatic three-arm exponent for critical planar percolation through the exact spectral threshold of an explicit positive integral operator family with elementary kernels, obtaining $ξ_3=0.76928375\cdots$. Unlike the monochromatic two-arm (backbone) event, the three-arm event can be obstructed by two distinct white clusters, so a Markovian exploration must retain the past connections. We introduce a two-point boundary observable that records these connections. Using the coupling between… — Gefei Cai — arXiv: sle

item.title: An Optimal Seed Reveals the Dynamical Route to Spontaneous Splitting of Turbulent Puffs
item.description: The localized turbulence in pipe flow, known as puffs, is sustained by their proliferation. This process is crucial to the subcritical laminar-turbulent transition, a century-old fundamental problem related to a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Here, we leverage the nonlinear nonmodal analysis of a reduced-order model to capture the full Navier-Stokes dynamics of the splitting process: from the splitting seed through the edge state to successful splitting, even when the pre-edge evolution is obscured… — Chihang Liu, Hao Ni, Jiashun Guan — arXiv: navier

item.title: Global weak solutions with vacuum for isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the unit disk under Dirichlet boundary conditions
item.description: We construct global weak solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson systems in the unit disk under no-slip boundary conditions, allowing vacuum and unbounded densities for sufficiently small initial energy. Such solutions particularly possess uniform $L^{q_0}$ density bounds for some $q_0>4γ$, beyond the natural energy class. Our analysis combines Green function representations with the mean-value property of harmonic functions to isolate a pressure-generated harmonic… — Shuai Wang, Xin Zhong — arXiv: navier

item.title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
item.description: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram… — Christopher Hughes, Somin Kim — arXiv: random matrix / arXiv: riemann

item.title: $L^1$ amplification near a self-similar vortex collapse in 2D Navier-Stokes
item.description: We establish quantitative $L^1$ instability for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse as viscosity tends to zero. For every $0<γ<\frac12$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, we construct solutions that are $O(ν^{1-γ})$-close in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ at $t_0$ but exhibit order-one $L^1$ separation in a shrinking neighborhood of the collapse point at times approaching collapse as $ν\to0$. By time translation, we also obtain pairs of solutions with initial $L^1$ distance $O(ν^{1-γ})$… — Trinh T. Nguyen — arXiv: navier

item.title: Global existence and uniqueness of Lions' weak solutions for the 2D inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations in bounded domains
item.description: The global well-posedness for Lions' weak solutions to the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two-dimensional bounded domains is concerned. When the initial density $0\leq ρ_0\in L^\infty(\Om)$ (allowing for vacuum) and initial velocity $u_0\in L^2_σ(Ω)$, the global existence, regularity, and exponential decay-in-time rates of weak solutions are established via a priori estimates, which rely crucially on the duality of BMO and Hardy space for the pressure term, and the classical Sobolev… — Hongyu Wang — arXiv: navier

item.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
item.description: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and… — Kailun Chen — arXiv: kpz prob

item.title: Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation
item.description: We prove that in rotationally invariant first-passage percolation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\geq2$, the passage time $T_n$ over a distance $n$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\exp(|T_n-μn|/n^{\frac{1}{2}(1-\varepsilon)})]\leq C$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, where $μ$ is the time constant. This implies that its variance is at most a constant times $n^{1-\varepsilon}$, the bound that Basu, Sidoravicius and Sly proved in the planar case. As in their work, our argument is an induction on the scale, but in place of their proof that… — Scott Armstrong, Ahmed Bou-Rabee — arXiv: lean

item.title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
item.description: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic… — Christopher Bunting — arXiv: navier

item.title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
item.description: A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above… — Johannes Bäumler, Tom Hutchcroft — arXiv: sle
